_note: The five distribution networks the player lays by hand. Each is a set of LINKS (cables, pipes, ducts) between the buildings named in `connects`; a link costs `linkCost` per level it spans (at least one) and may span at most `maxSpanLevels`. HUBS are the buildings that hand the network out to everything within their serviceRadiusLevels (catalog/buildings/*.json): a junction lights the rooms around it, a cistern waters them, a duct fan airs them — but a hub only works when it is linked back to where the network comes from. The graph is read by systems/infrastructure/networkGraph.js; each system settles its own network over it. A network not listed in config infrastructure.enforced is treated as fully laid (every node joined, every hub reaching everywhere) — which is how system tests isolate one network at a time.

networks.name: Power grid
networks.description: Generators feed junctions by cable; each junction lights every room within its reach, up to its capacity. When the generators run short, junctions are served in priority order (1 first) and batteries cover only the junctions they are cabled to.
networks._note: Loss scales with cable run from the generator plus the drop from the junction to the room, so a shallow level fed from a deep generator pays for every level of cable between.

networks.name: Water mains
networks.description: Pumps and the reclamation plant feed cisterns by pipe; each cistern stores water and supplies every room and resident within its reach. A purifier on the mains cleans the reclaimed water that passes through it.
networks._note: Pumping upward costs power proportional to lift height, so water costs more the higher people live.

networks.name: Sewer
networks.description: What a cistern's rooms and residents use comes back dirty. Drains carry it downhill only, cistern to cistern, to a reclamation plant; sewage with nowhere to go is dumped where it was made and fouls that level's air.
networks._note: Gravity is the whole design: a drain never carries anything up, so the plant belongs at the bottom.

networks.name: Air ducts
networks.description: Each duct fan either sucks or blows. Air drawn in by the sucking fans travels the ducts to the blowing ones, cleaned by every scrubber and freshened by every oxygen garden it passes, and is blown out onto the levels they reach. Nothing moves unless a group has both. A scrubber or garden off the air's path works on its own level only.
networks._note: Airflow is settled in systems/airQuality/airflow.js. Suck where the air is foul (the Works), route it through the scrubbers and gardens, blow it where people live. Sealing a level cuts it from every fan.
